article.headline: Prime Minister Mark Carney Warns Foreign Nations Against Meddling In Alberta Referendum
article.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney urges Albertans to vote in the upcoming October 19 referendum to ensure the integrity of the process against foreign interference.
article.body:
Leading figures in the separatist movement have traveled to the United States seeking assistance, with U.S. officials Scott Bessent and Howard Lutnik openly discussing Alberta as a potential partner or commenting on federal trade talks. Prime Minister Mark Carney told Global News that national security agencies are actively monitoring for covert foreign interference, though he declined to provide specific details regarding those investigations.    The upcoming vote is critical as it will decide whether Alberta initiates the legal process to hold a binding referendum on separation from Canada. The outcome of this decision carries significant weight for provincial politics, where the separatist debate has remained a dominant issue for more than a year. Carney emphasized that the most effective defense against outside influence is for residents to participate directly in the democratic process.

Speaking in Calgary, Carney stated that Ottawa has made it absolutely clear that foreign governments must remain uninvolved in domestic elections. He positioned voting as a fundamental duty for Albertans to ensure their own voices define the province's future. During his visit to the province, the Prime Minister highlighted recent federal investments, including the Pacific Link pipeline project intended for the British Columbia coast, as part of his administration's commitment to Alberta.

In addition to the separation question, ballots include five distinct immigration inquiries. While a rally in Calgary highlighted immigration as a central theme, Calgary Mayor Jeromy Farkas was the only official at the event to explicitly call for a "No" vote on the remaining nine items appearing on the ballot.

article.headline: Benfica Routs Celtic 4-1 as Scottish Champions Struggle in Europe League
article.summary: Celtic remain winless in the Europa League after suffering a 4-1 defeat away to Benfica in Lisbon.
article.body:
Celtic were effectively out of the contest by halftime, trailing 3-0 after a series of defensive errors left the Scottish side facing a mountain to climb. The visitors handed Benfica an early lead just four minutes into the match when Dane Murray conceded a penalty, which Jhon Duran converted. Alexander Bah added a second before Jhon Duran scored his brace, leaving Celtic 34th out of 36 teams in the competition standings after two matches. While Camilo Duran pulled a goal back for the visitors after the break, Vangelis Pavlidis eventually sealed the comprehensive win for the hosts with a late fourth goal.

The loss marks Celtic's fourth defeat in their past five matches across all competitions. For manager Martin O'Neill, the result underscores a difficult start to the European campaign, as his side has now lost both of their opening group matches. Despite the outcome, O'Neill expressed optimism regarding his team's second-half performance, insisting that the attacking display provides a foundation for the remainder of the league phase.

According to the BBC, the scoreline accurately reflected the disparity between the two sides, as Benfica dominated possession and hit the woodwork multiple times throughout the encounter. Captain Callum McGregor acknowledged that unforced errors were the primary cause of the collapse, noting that the team failed to manage the ball effectively at the top level. Although Celtic managed to create several chances in the second half, they were consistently punished by a clinical Benfica side that remained superior in both halves of play. The defeat leaves Celtic searching for their first points of the European season as they prepare for upcoming fixtures.
